heroHeadline: HIMARS Deadline Day (May 31): PLA Drops to 1 Sortie After May 30 16-Sortie Surge — 8 PLAN Vessels + 4 Ships Sustain Maritime Pressure; NT$8.81B Budget PASSED May 29 (HIMARS, M109A7, Anti-Armor Drones Funded); May 30: 16 Sorties (7/16 Cross Median N/E ADIZ); Full May Sequence: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7→6→16→4→9→26→10→9→10→16→1
heroSubtitle: May 31, 2026 is Taiwan's HIMARS first payment deadline: the NT$800 million down payment on 82 HIMARS launchers is due today. Taiwan's Legislative Yuan passed the NT$8.81B FY2026 special arms procurement budget on its third reading on May 29 without opposition, and the Executive Yuan had pre-authorized emergency reserve funds as a payment backstop — positioning Taiwan to meet the deadline. On May 31, Taiwan's MND detected only 1 PLA aircraft sortie (a dramatic 94% drop from May 30's 16-sortie surge) while 8 PLAN vessels and 4 official ships continued to operate around Taiwan — maintaining maritime pressure even as air activity collapsed to near-zero. May 30 had seen 16 sorties with 7 crossing the median line into northern and eastern ADIZ sectors, coming one day after the budget passage. The full May 2026 sortie sequence now reads: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7→6→16→4→9→26→10→9→10→16→1. The May 31 pullback is consistent with the established PLA spike-then-pullback oscillation documented throughout the month. The NT$8.81B FY2026 budget funds: 82 HIMARS launchers (NT$2.8B), M109A7 self-propelled howitzers (NT$3.9B), anti-armor drone systems (NT$1.8B), Javelin ATGMs, and TOW 2B anti-armor missiles; the legislation also authorizes up to NT$780 billion in total US arms procurement through 2033. Defense Minister Wellington Koo confirmed HIMARS provides Taiwan with 300 km deep-strike capability against PLA missile platforms. US FMS pause for Operation Epic Fury (Iran) remains active; the $14B PAC-3/NASAMS package remains 'in abeyance' (Trump); no Trump-Lai direct call has been confirmed. The US autonomous uncrewed surface vessel 'Lightfish' completed the first autonomous Taiwan Strait transit in late May 2026.
